claim: For autumn 2027 the first admissions round opens 16 October 2026 and closes 15 January 2027, with supporting documentation due 1 February and bachelor results published 8 April. The second round runs 15 March to 15 April 2027, with results on 9 July.
excerpt: First admissions round … 16 October 2026 Application round opens. 15 January 2027 Application deadline + last day to rank your courses. 1 February Supporting documentation deadline. 8 April Admissions results published for Bachelor's. […] Second admissions round … 15 March 2027 Application round opens. 15 April Application deadline. 21 June Supporting documentation deadline. 9 July Admissions results published. 16 July Last day to reply to your offer.
interpretation: The two rounds are not equivalent and the difference decides the year for an IB applicant. The first round is the one carrying the English-taught programmes; the authority says of the second that "many courses and programmes taught in English are no longer available for application". So the real deadline for an international applicant is 15 January, with documents by 1 February — five months before IB results are published on 6 July.

claim: General entry to a Swedish bachelor requires completed upper secondary education, English to the level of Swedish English 6, and mathematics to the level of Swedish Mathematics 1a/1b/1c. Specific requirements are set per programme.
excerpt: To meet the general entry requirements for bachelor's studies, you must: have successfully completed your upper secondary (high school) education (post-16), and be able to demonstrate proficiency in English. The entry requirement for bachelor's studies in Sweden is to have studied the equivalent of the Swedish upper secondary course English 6/English Level 2. For applicants who received their final school grades after 31 December 2009, there is an additional mathematics requirement. […] The equivalents listed are estimates.
interpretation: The authority labels its own subject equivalences as estimates, which is unusual and worth repeating rather than smoothing over. An IB student should treat a published IB-to-Swedish subject mapping as a guide and confirm against the programme.
